correction.text: Ceredigion and Carmarthenshire (Dinefwr): the realm after the Lord Rhys, with Ceredigion under Maelgwn ap Rhys

keyframe_review.note: [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Ceredigion stays in the shape. The earlier 1197 loss of Ceredigion to the Normans quoted 'Following his death, most of Deheubarth was taken over by the Normans', which on the Rhys ap Gruffydd page sits in the lead's paragraph about Rhys ap Tewdwr (killed 1093), not about the Lord Rhys (died 28 April 1197); for 1197 the page says only that Maelgwn 'took the town and castle of Aberystwyth and captured Gruffudd', and nothing puts Ceredigion in Norman hands. The loss is dropped (and marcher-lordships' 1197 gain and 1283 loss of Ceredigion with it), so that the Principality's 1283 gain of Ceredigion and Carmarthenshire from this state is consistent. Earlier note: the page does not place the rump; Carmarthenshire (Dinefwr, the capital) is the researcher's reading; the lineage list gives Maelgwn ap Rhys (1199-1230) for Ceredigion.

region.text: Gwynedd, after Idwal Foel and Elisedd were killed by Edmund's forces

ledger.note: 942: Hywel Dda takes Gwynedd. 'Idwal and his brother Elisedd were both killed in battle in 942 against Edmund's forces'; Hywel 'established himself as ruler over Gwynedd'.
942: Powys with Gwynedd. 'This probably placed him in control of the Kingdom of Powys.' The page hedges.

region.text: Gwynedd, to the sons of Idwal

ledger.note: 950: Hywel dies and the realm splits. 'Following Hywel's death in 949 or 950, his kingdom was soon split into three'; Gwynedd went to Iago and Ieuaf, Deheubarth and Powys to Hywel's sons.
950: Powys leaves the realm. The page gives Powys to Hywel's sons but lists the Powys successor as 'disputed'; Cliopatria draws Powys separately from 960.

1163: Henry II strips Rhys of everything. 'Henry invaded Deheubarth in 1163, stripped Rhys of all his lands and took him prisoner.'

certainty.note: The pages give counties and cantrefi, not borders; the 942-950 expansion and the post-1197 rump are the softest.

notes: Cliopatria has a row Kingdom of Seisyllwg 878-959 (slug kingdom-of-seisyllwg, another part of eu-11); it is Seisyllwg until 920 and Deheubarth after, so that dossier and this one overlap in 920-959 and the reviewer should treat them as one state. Seisyllwg page: infobox changed name from Ceredigion 680; Ystrad Tywi taken from Dyfed in the late 7th century; Gwgon of Ceredigion drowned 872 and Rhodri Mawr 'became steward over the realm' (the Rhodri Mawr page does not say he took it); Cadell died about 909 or 911, his lands divided between Hywel and Clydog; merger with Dyfed 920. The infobox disestablishes Deheubarth in 1197; this dossier runs to 1283 because the page itself says 'From 1234 to 1283, Deheubarth was subject to the princes of Gwynedd' and the Gwynedd dossier pairs a vassal_start 1259 and vassal_end 1277 with the counterpart 'deheubarth' (the page dates the subjection from 1234; the Gwynedd dossier from 1259: a disagreement for the reviewer). Gwynedd and Powys dossiers name kingdom-of-seisyllwg as Hywel Dda's realm of 942-950; it should read deheubarth. The 1171 Justiciarship of South Wales and the 1267 Treaty of Montgomery are vassal relations of the Angevin and English dossiers; the Treaty of Aberconwy is undated on the Deheubarth page (1277 on Gwynedd's). Brycheiniog 'was also added' (undated) and is not in the keyframes; the Brycheiniog dossier covers its own shapes. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] After the review: the 1197 loss of Ceredigion to marcher-lordships is dropped (its quoted sentence is about Rhys ap Tewdwr and 1093, re-checked on the Rhys ap Gruffydd page; for 1197 the page says only that Rhys 'died on 28 April 1197' and Maelgwn 'took the town and castle of Aberystwyth and captured Gruffudd'), Ceredigion stays in the 1197-1282 keyframe, and the vassal pair and the 1283 dissolve cover Ceredigion and Carmarthenshire. This agrees with principality-of-wales' 1283 gain of both counties from this state. Disagreements left: the 1234-1283 subjection to Gwynedd against kingdom-of-gwynedd's 1259-1277 is for the Gwynedd owner; angevin-empire (other group) has no mirror of the 1158, 1163 and 1165 events; kingdom-of-powys and the Gwynedd dossier name kingdom-of-seisyllwg for 942-950 where the Deheubarth page says Hywel's realm.
